T: Old trees, taller than anything in the Archive. The air smells of rain and pine.
F: A split-rail fence, grey with age. Someone mends it now and then.
S: A signpost. One arm points back the way you came. The other, east, reads only: ONWARD.
c: A candle in an iron lantern, burning steadily at the roadside. It feels like the Archive's candles. Somehow, it feels safe.
K: A cocoon, half hidden in the long grass at the roadside. A leather satchel strap pokes out of the silk.
Whoever is inside was going somewhere in a hurry.
The silk won't give. Not yet.
=: The great door of the Archive, set into a hill of old stone. From out here, it looks like it has always been part of the hill.
>: The road runs on east toward distant towers.
